defects.title: With two different gene lists the growth rates are written to the transposed position of the result matrix, so pairs get the growth rate of another pair
defects.trigger: doubleGeneDeletion(model, 'FBA', {'g1'; 'g2'}, {'g3'; 'g4'}) on the toy model EX_A ( -> A, ub 10), R1 (A -> B, ub 4, rule g1), R2 (A -> B, rule g2), R3 (B -> C, rule g3), R4 (B -> C, ub 6, rule g4), BIO (C -> , objective)
defects.observed: (R2025a, gurobi, 2026-11-25) grRateKO = [6 4; 4 4]: entry (1,2) (pair g1-g4) holds 4, the rate of pair g2-g3; lines 167/170 and 179 also write each rate to (geneNo2, geneNo1), the position of pair geneList1{geneNo2}-geneList2{geneNo1}, and a later pair overwrites the correct value

notes: Repro (MATLAB after initCobraToolbox, gurobi): m = createModel({'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'R3';'R4';'BIO'}, {'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'R3';'R4';'BIO'}, {' -> A';'A -> B';'A -> B';'B -> C';'B -> C';'C -> '}, 'upperBoundList', [10 4 1000 1000 6 1000], 'grRuleList', {'';'g1';'g2';'g3';'g4';''}, 'printLevel', 0); m = changeObjective(m, 'BIO'); [~, ko] = doubleGeneDeletion(m, 'FBA', {'g1';'g2'}, {'g3';'g4'}) -> [6 4; 4 4] (expected [6 10; 4 4]); the one-list call doubleGeneDeletion(m, 'FBA') gives the correct symmetric 4x4 matrix [10 0 6 10; 0 4 4 4; 6 4 6 0; 10 4 0 10]. The defect is confined to the call form with a non-empty geneList2 (differentSetsFlag); no src file calls doubleGeneDeletion (grep), so the lead may seed it NONE. Callees: it calls singleGeneDeletion with 4 inputs (uniqueGene default 0, avoids its seed) and linearMOMA only for method 'lMOMA'. Further observations (not recorded): line 131 saves doubleGeneDeletionTmp.mat into the current folder every 1000 pairs (side effect); the existing multi-function legacy test testDeletionStudy.m also calls it (not renamed).
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: with two different gene lists the rates land in the transposed cell (writer reproduced); no src caller

notes: Hand-built 5-reaction model (createModel, no addReaction) with two blocked reactions; eco hand-built with only .model. Existing multi-function test testEcosystemToy.m also calls it (not renamed). 100% coverage.

Hand-built two-member community (6 reactions, yield 1) and eco structure (model, objectives, memberRxns, points, feasiblePoints); every value derived by hand: closest feasible point selection (infeasible point skipped, y outer loop), member normalization (/f and /(1-f)), community reaction not normalized, updateBounds false, both error messages. The try/catch NaN branch (lines 133-134) is reached with gurobi only: a free cycle reaction with infinite bounds has FVA range [-Inf, Inf] with gurobi, and fixing it to +-Inf makes the inner FVA fail; glpk raises an error for the unbounded FVA before the loop (fluxVariability 'A Solution could not be found'), so that section is gated to gurobi (comment in the test). Existing multi-function tests testEcosystemToy.m/testEcosystemScenarios.m also call it. 100% coverage.

Two hand-built toy models with different reaction sets; expected KO objective fluxes derived by hand; table rows (sorted union), numeric values and 'NotIncluded'; dataStruct fields, grRateKO, and every fluxSolution column checked (S*v = 0, bounds, zero flux on the deleted reaction, OBJ flux = grRateKO); folder input with a dotted file name ('model.one.mat' -> modelone_model) and another variable name. Lines 63-64 exempt: unreachable (singleRxnDeletion(model) returns delRxn = model.rxns, so the setdiff is always empty). gurobi and glpk. Cosmetic observations not recorded: line 55 uses the model name as an fprintf format; line 63 prints 'Warning:' with fprintf and line 64 is a no-op statement (modelNames{j}; without output).

defects.title: The help text gives a wrong usage and an input that does not exist
defects.observed: USAGE shows guidedSim(model, fvaType, rl), INPUTS list solver, and the description says the solver is set to 'cplex'; the function is guidedSim(model, rl) and does not change the solver
defects.expected: USAGE guidedSim(model, rl) and the inputs model and rl only

notes: Toy model with ranges independent of the objective fraction (99.99 vs 99.999). On this machine fastFVA runs (a cplexFVA binary works although getCobraSolverVersion reports CPLEX 'undetermined' and ibm_cplex is not an installed COBRA solver), so lines 30-35 are reached here; an infeasible model gives ret ~= 0 -> NaN (lines 33-34). The fallback to fluxVariability is forced by a reaction list not in model order (fastFVA errors 'Your input reaction vector is not sorted'), and the FBA fallback by that list on an infeasible model (optimizeCbModel f = NaN). Assertions hold whether or not fastFVA runs (CI without CPLEX takes the fallbacks). fastFVA calls rng('shuffle') and cd(CBTDIR): the test saves/restores rng; guidedSim cds back. fastFVA (src/analysis/FVA/fastFVA/fastFVA.m) is called on every input (static call, has testFastFVA.m; not added to extra_edges). 100% coverage.

defects.title: The solver option is ignored; the current LP solver is always used
defects.trigger: ensureWBMfeasibility(folder, 'solver', 'glpk') while CBT_LP_SOLVER is gurobi; folder is an empty temporary folder
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-25) CBT_LP_SOLVER is still 'gurobi' after the call: with CBT_LP_SOLVER non-empty the else branch sets solver = CBT_LP_SOLVER whatever the option, then changeCobraSolver(solver, 'LP') selects gurobi; the elseif (line 55) is unreachable (same isempty test as line 53)
defects.expected: the models are solved with the solver given by the option ('solver: LP solver to use (default '''', i.e. the current solver)'), i.e. glpk

notes: Repro (MATLAB after initCobraToolbox, changeCobraSolver('gurobi','LP')): global CBT_LP_SOLVER; d = tempname; mkdir(d); ensureWBMfeasibility(d, 'solver', 'glpk'); disp(CBT_LP_SOLVER) -> gurobi (writes dietGrowthStats.xlsx into d; rmdir(d,'s') after). Further suspected defects found by reading, NOT probed (they need whole-body models): (a) line 256 'while ~feasible && all(cell2mat(updatedDietComponentsTmp(:,2)) <= -10)' is inverted (comment: do not allow bounds below -10; values start above -10, e.g. -0.1 from line 243), so the step-3 bound search never runs (wrong-result); (b) line 233 'for j = 1:length(dietaryMetsConsumed)' uses length of an N x 2 cell, i.e. max(N, 2): with N = 1 it runs j = 2 and indexes a missing row (error); (c) line 242 indexes updatedDietComponents(end,2) when it may be empty (no single culprit reaction) -> error; (d) checkWbmFormat (lines 518, 527) calls warning('off') then warning('on'), which turns on every warning that was off before (global side effect, VII-B); (e) with an empty folder (all models feasible) it prints 'No diet could be found for which all WBMs can grow' (cosmetic). Default optimizeWBModel method is LP (minNorm 0), so the optimizeWBModel QPold seed is not reached. Callees loadMinimalWBM, setDietConstraints (called with Diet name string, avoids its seed), getMissingDietPersephone are reached only with model files.
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: the 'solver' option is ignored (writer reproduced); default reach; four further suspected defects need whole-body models and are left unprobed (notes)

defects.title: Every call fails because the diet function setFoodConstraints no longer exists
defects.trigger: any call with at least one diet, e.g. compareDietPerformance(model, {{'A', 1}}, {'R1'})
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-25) MATLAB:UndefinedFunction "Undefined function 'setFoodConstraints' for input arguments of type 'struct'." at line 69; no setFoodConstraints.m exists in the repository (removed in commit 96e7677895 'Overhaul of nutrition toolbox')
defects.expected: a table with the min and max flux of each reaction of interest under each diet

notes: Repro (MATLAB after initCobraToolbox): m = createModel({'EX_A';'R1';'BIO'}, {'EX_A';'R1';'BIO'}, {' -> A';'A -> B';'B -> '}, 'printLevel', 0); compareDietPerformance(m, {{'A', 1}}, {'R1'}) -> Undefined function 'setFoodConstraints'. Reached by every call with a non-empty diets cell (an empty diets cell would skip the loop and reach cell2table on an empty array). Also noted, not probed: line 70 constrains 'Excretion_EX_microbiota_LI_biomass' without the [fe] suffix used elsewhere (ensureWBMfeasibility line 558), so on WBMs it would warn and not constrain. The fix likely needs the diet function setDietConstraints or a restored setFoodConstraints; lead decision.
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: every call fails: setFoodConstraints is not in the repository (lead checked); default reach

defects.title: Without an experiment the solver generation fails in Perl
defects.trigger: generateIsotopomerSolver(model, 'xglcDe') (no experiment; the help lists experiment among the inputs, the code treats it as optional via nargin > 2)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-25) IsotopomerModel.txt is written without measured metabolites, then perl(generatorEMU.pl) fails: 'outputs file not found.  assuming everything is output / should not get here because outputs must be known'; the working folder is left at the c13solver folder of src (the cd back is not reached)
defects.expected: experiment required (an error saying so), or the call works without it

notes: Tiny hand-built 5-reaction isotopomer model (not model.mat): expected IsotopomerModel.txt lines derived by hand (v<index> insertion, '!' split, measured fragments, default inputMet xglcDe, BLK left out by FVAflag, NOMAP with empty mapping skipped); the 5 generated solver files are checked by reading their function line (last input = xglcDe), never executed. Error branch line 94 reached by temporarily making a folder named IsotopomerModel.txt in src (removed at once). Backup/restore: the 6 generated files present before are copied to a tempname folder and copied back, every new file in the folder is deleted; verified md5-identical after the run. Requires perl (prepareTest requiredSoftwares outside Windows). Skipped input: the two-input call (limitation above); skipping it leaves no line uncovered. 100% coverage, ~3 s.
